purpose: Trabectedin is a chemotherapy medicine used to treat certain types of soft tissue sarcoma, which is a cancer that grows in the soft tissues of the body like muscles, fat, or connective tissue. It is typically used when the cancer has spread or cannot be removed with surgery, and when other treatments have already been tried. In some countries it is also used for ovarian cancer.
how_it_works: Think of your DNA as a very detailed instruction manual inside each cell. Trabectedin works by attaching itself to the DNA in cancer cells and damaging it so badly that the cancer cells can no longer copy themselves or grow. This essentially puts the brakes on the cancer spreading. Because cancer cells divide much more rapidly than most normal cells, they are more vulnerable to this kind of damage.
common_side_effects: Some common side effects include nausea, vomiting, fatigue, and loss of appetite. You may notice swelling, constipation, or diarrhea. Your blood counts may drop, making you more tired or more likely to get infections or bruise easily. Liver enzyme levels in your blood may also go up, which your doctor will monitor with regular blood tests.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious liver problems, so your doctor will check your liver regularly with blood tests. It can also seriously lower your white and red blood cell counts, increasing your risk of infections and bleeding — contact your doctor right away if you develop a fever. Trabectedin can cause muscle breakdown (a condition called rhabdomyolysis), which is serious and needs immediate medical attention. It must be given through a vein (IV) in a medical setting and should never be used if you are pregnant, as it can harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as many drugs can interact with trabectedin.
typical_dosing: Trabectedin is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion directly into your vein through a central line or port — it is NOT a pill you take at home. The usual dose is given once every 3 weeks, and each infusion takes about 24 hours to complete in a clinical setting. Your doctor will calculate the exact dose based on your body size and will adjust it if you experience side effects.
